definitions.explanation: The soft tissue of the body.

examples.japanese: {焼肉|やきにく}を{食|た}べに{行|い}きませんか。
examples.english: Shall we go eat grilled meat?

examples.japanese: {牛肉|ぎゅうにく}と{豚肉|ぶたにく}、どちらが{好|す}きですか。
examples.english: Which do you prefer, beef or pork?

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}の{肉|にく}はとても{柔|やわ}らかくて{美味|おい}しいと{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: This restaurant is famous for its tender and delicious meat.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}では{焼肉|やきにく}やすき{焼|や}きなど{色々|いろいろ}な{肉料理|にくりょうり}があって、{季節|きせつ}ごとに{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: In Japan, there are many kinds of meat dishes like grilled meat and sukiyaki that can be enjoyed in every season.

examples.japanese: {運動|うんどう}で{筋肉|きんにく}がついた。
{歳|とし}を{取|と}ると{体|からだ}の{肉|にく}が{落|お}ちやすくなる。
examples.english: As you get older, you tend to lose body mass more easily.

examples.japanese: {傷|きず}の{部分|ぶぶん}の{肉|にく}が{盛|も}り{上|あ}がってきて、だいぶ{良|よ}くなってきた。
examples.english: The flesh around the wound has started to grow back, and it's getting much better.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{走|はし}ったり{泳|およ}いだりして{体|からだ}を{動|うご}かしていたら、{腕|うで}や{足|あし}の{筋肉|きんにく}がしっかりついてきた。
examples.english: Since I've been running and swimming every day to stay active, my arms and legs have become much more muscular.

notes:
{肉|にく} refers to meat (for food) or flesh (body tissue).

TYPES OF MEAT:
- {牛肉|ぎゅうにく}: beef
- {豚肉|ぶたにく}: pork
- {鶏肉|とりにく}/{鳥肉|とりにく}: chicken
- {羊肉|ようにく}: lamb, mutton
- {馬肉|ばにく}: horse meat

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {焼肉|やきにく}: grilled meat (Korean-style BBQ)
- {肉屋|にくや}: butcher shop
- {筋肉|きんにく}: muscle
- {肉料理|にくりょうり}: meat dishes
- ひき{肉|にく}: ground meat

USAGE NOTE:
When used alone, {肉|にく} often defaults to beef or pork depending on context. In casual speech, people may say お{肉|にく} with the polite prefix.
